report:
Baseline: independently compared the current whole-file fragments for expr.rs and semantic_spec.rs with both historical implementation_sources and test_sources; every comparison is an exact line-array match. The captured prior report correctly describes partial implementation, rather than completed coverage.

Fresh assessment: the complete claim requires available expectations at the expression-checking boundary, permits local inference and explicit coercion, and forbids using expectations to select trait-proof, method-provider, or alias-normalization candidates. The ordinary expr.rs association supplies the initial boundary: direct calls obtain parameter types before checking each argument and pass the corresponding type to check_with_expected; absent parameter information falls back to synthesis. check_with_expected itself synthesizes with check_with first and only then calls the coercion API. Blocks, closures, tuples, arrays and branches likewise synthesize nested expressions without receiving the caller expectation. Thus recursive consumption is demonstrably incomplete, exactly as the second implementation association in semantic_spec.rs declares. The call sites demonstrate requested coercion, not a claim here that every conversion or independent solver behavior is implemented.

The complete associated test set is the single TODO sage_meta::todo::checking_body_expected_types. Its empty body has no behavioral assertions and cannot detect expectation propagation, conversion, or candidate-selection regressions. Its explicit matrix defers representative arguments, literals, closures, aggregate/branch elements, completed-IR conversions, and incompatible expectations against ambiguous solver/method candidates. Solver independence includes normalization as well as trait proof under the complete claim; neither that requirement nor method-provider independence is promoted to verified implementation by this review. Prerequisites are recursive expression-specific expectation consumption and source-driven fixtures checking typed output and independent candidate results, including ambiguous normalization. This is adequate explicit accounting for the present unfinished slice. No N/A entries exist; no edits are required to retain the justified TODO status.

Evidence and execution: reviewed current claim, both implementation entries and their whole-file context, and the complete annotated test body; captured the review specification with review read. No additional implementation helpers were relied on to assert completed behavior. Ran review start and exact-baseline comparisons; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing sage-meta tests and a passing root build, which do not establish this deferred claim.
